re_line: DPRK constitution published · North Korea fires 2 ballistic missiles · Cho-Rubio meet in Paris · Bond dealers fined record $1.2B · Congress post-midterm reshuffles
morning_memo: Naenara published the full text of the March 2026 revised DPRK constitution, formalizing Kim Jong Un's expanded powers and the two-state territorial definition.

imagery_report.label: 38 North analysis: Choe Hyon destroyer strategic implications
imagery_report.headline: 38 North publishes detailed analysis of North Korea's Choe Hyon surface warship and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet
imagery_report.body: 38 North's analysis examines the Choe Hyon destroyer, North Korea's most capable surface combatant, detailing its weapons loadout including cruise missiles and its role within the West Sea Fleet. The piece assesses the vessel's strategic significance in the context of North Korea's accelerating naval modernization, which has included Kim Jong Un's Nov 7-8 inspection of a new warship under construction at Nampho Shipyard. The analysis connects to 38 North's Oct 30 report documenting public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine.

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after 2+ years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: 38 North satellite imagery from October 16 confirms trucks traversing the New Yalu River (DPRK-Friendship) Bridge one day after the October 15 official opening, marking the start of commercial vehicle traffic. Daily NK reports (Oct 31) that North Korean trucks have still not joined Chinese cargo trucks on the bridge two weeks after the Oct 15 opening; North Korean transport officials are still preparing vehicles. North Korea-China trade reached $299M in September 2026, the second-highest monthly total in 2026. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reports on Nov 3, 2026 that North Korea is courting Chinese investors to build hotels and shopping complexes in Sinuiju. NK News reports a surge in North Korean delegations visiting China, putting commercial ties in focus.

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Navy fired approximately 60 warning shots; vessel retreated after 1 hour. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands, with Seoul stepping up surveillance along the maritime border. 38 North satellite imagery published October 29 shows North Korea continuing to install new fencing along its border. North Korean propaganda loudspeakers were visible at two border locations on Nov 4 from Odusan Unification Observatory and Key Observatory in Gyeonggi Province. ROK Joint Chiefs confirmed Nov 6 that a drifting North Korean fishing vessel was spotted in international waters off Ulleung Island on Nov 3 and is under investigation.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

top_stories.headline: North Korea fires two ballistic missiles from Muncheon; Naenara publishes revised constitution text
top_stories.body: North Korea launched two ballistic missiles from Muncheon into the East Sea on Nov 11, with a flight distance of approximately 350 km, according to JTBC and Yonhap reporting. Separately, North Korea's official web portal Naenara published the full text of the constitution amended by the Supreme People's Assembly on March 23, 2026, formalizing **Kim Jong Un**'s expanded authority and the country's redefinition of its territory to exclude the South, the first time the constitution section had been restored to the portal since North Korea pledged to rewrite the document in early 2024, per NK News. The launch is the latest in a series of weapons tests over the past week, all of which have been kept off the domestic news agenda.

top_stories.headline: FM Cho Hyun meets SecState Rubio on G7 sidelines; agrees to advance Lee-Trump summit agreements
top_stories.body: ROK Foreign Minister **Cho Hyun** held a bilateral meeting with US Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** on Nov 10 on the sidelines of the G7 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Paris, exchanging views on overall bilateral relations, high-level exchanges, and North Korea, according to MOFA. Rubio separately noted at a press conference that South Korea was among the partners invited to the G7 meeting.

also_today.headline: North Korea lists its Mexico City embassy building for sale at over $2 million
also_today.body_text: NK News confirmed the DPRK flag and identifying plaque were removed from the building's exterior and a for-sale sign now hangs above the entrance, though staff remain on-site and the mission is described as still operational. The move adds to a pattern of DPRK embassy closures and downsizing across Latin America and Europe amid sanctions pressure and budgetary constraints.

also_today.headline: Czech Republic restores Pyongyang embassy, makes Karel Srol new ambassador
also_today.body_text: **Karel Srol** took up his post as Czech ambassador to North Korea in October, more than five years after Prague suspended embassy operations during the pandemic, making the Czech Republic the fifth EU member state to restore a diplomatic presence in Pyongyang. Srol paid a courtesy call on the Chinese ambassador to North Korea, Wang Yajun, upon arrival.

also_today.headline: North Korean reunites with family member in South in first such case in two years
also_today.body_text: In April, the ROK Unification Ministry received a request through a North Korean defector from an individual in the DPRK seeking to locate an uncle living in the South, leading to a rare reunion, the first such case in two years. New data cited in the report shows over three-quarters of South Koreans separated from family in the North have already died.

also_today.headline: Defense ministry revises military academy merger plan; Army academy to relocate to Chungcheong
also_today.body_text: The Ministry of National Defense briefed lawmakers on a revised plan to relocate the Korea Military Academy to the Chungcheong region while retaining the Naval Academy in Jinhae and the Air Force Academy in Cheongju, backing away from the July proposal to merge all three into Daejeon's Jaundae compound. The revised plan adopts a 1-2-1 curricular model with shared first and final years at a joint academy, with implementation expected from the 2029 academic year.

also_today.headline: Seoul pledges $20 million to ADB Korea AI for Development Trust Fund
also_today.body_text: The Ministry of Finance and Economy signed a contribution agreement with the Asian Development Bank at their annual consultation meeting in Seoul, pledging *$20 million* to the Korea AI for Development Trust Fund, which will support the Center for AI Innovation and Development to be established in South Korea under a May agreement with the ADB.

also_today.headline: Ruling and opposition parties reach tentative deal to delay digital asset tax until 2029
also_today.body_text: A National Assembly finance subcommittee including lawmakers from both the ruling Democratic Party and opposition People Power Party reached a tentative consensus to delay South Korea's digital asset tax by two years to 2029, the fourth such postponement, per Yonhap. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il had proposed the two-year delay the prior week, citing preparation concerns.

overnight_items.body_text: Late-October transfers stirred resentment inside the spy agency that spent years developing the cadre.

us_korea_deals.state_of_play: Steel and aluminum remain at 50% and autos at 15%, both under Section 232 authority. The Section 122 surcharge expired July 24 2026, leaving no single baseline reciprocal tariff. Section 301 investigations launched March 11 2026 against South Korea and 15 other trading partners are now the primary prospective tariff vehicle.

business_economy.headline: South Korean battery makers face greater scrutiny in Hungary
business_economy.body_text: South Korean battery manufacturers operating in Hungary are facing heightened regulatory scrutiny, Bloomberg reports, as European governments increase oversight of foreign-invested industrial facilities. The development is relevant to LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK On, which have major European production investments.

business_economy.headline: South Korean firms win string of CES 2027 innovation awards
business_economy.body_text: LG Electronics won eight CES 2027 Innovation Awards including a Best of Innovation honor for its LG SIGNATURE OLED T, the world's first transparent wireless television, extending LG OLED TVs' run of Best of Innovation awards to five consecutive years dating back to 2023. Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution also received recognition for battery and software innovations.

northeast_asia.headline: North Korean envoy's Beijing visit fuels Kim Jong Un-Xi summit speculation
northeast_asia.body_text: Seoul's Foreign Ministry assessed that North Korean envoy **Kim Sung-nam**'s third Beijing visit was aimed at sharing results of a Chinese party meeting and maintaining high-level exchanges, rather than primarily arranging a summit.

northeast_asia.headline: FM Cho meets Canadian FM Anand; agrees to expand Canadian oil, LNG imports
northeast_asia.body_text: FM **Cho Hyun** met Canadian FM **Anita Anand** on Nov 10 in Paris and agreed to deepen cooperation in energy, specifically expanding imports of Canadian crude oil and LNG, as well as AI, critical minerals, and defense, one month after a phone call between the two ministers. The two sides described Canada and South Korea as 'comprehensive strategic partners.'

rok_government.action: MOFA hosts 8th Action with Women and Peace international conference in Seoul
rok_government.detail: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs convened the 8th Action with Women and Peace international conference at the Grand Lotte Seoul hotel on Nov 11, bringing together international organization representatives, academics, and civil society experts to discuss Women, Peace and Security innovation including AI applications. The initiative has been run by MOFA since 2019.

rok_government.action: Unification Minister describes North Korea's military provocations as 'signals' toward dialogue
rok_government.detail: Unification Minister **Chung Dong-young** stated that North Korea's military demonstrations are also signals directed at South Korea, and that reducing hostility is the core of the Lee government's peace policy. He said easing adversarial relations must come first before substantive dialogue can be pursued.

calendar_watch.headline: Korea Railroad Workers' Union begins indefinite general strike
calendar_watch.detail: The Korea Railroad Workers' Union announced an indefinite general strike beginning December 10 at 9 a.m., per Yonhap's headline summary.

rok_assembly.action: Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik outlines constitutional amendment framework excluding current president from re-election
rok_assembly.detail: National Assembly Speaker **Cho Jeong-sik** stated that barring the current president from re-election is a core principle of a sovereignty-based constitutional amendment, and that 2027, a year without scheduled elections, would be an appropriate and calm time to pursue revision, per Hankyoreh and other outlets.

social_statements.analyst_note: Rubio's public identification of South Korea as a G7 partner invitee follows the FM Cho-Rubio bilateral in which the two sides agreed to advance Lee-Trump summit implementation.

official_x_posts.analyst_note: The post accompanied the record 1.6 trillion won fine on 15 bond-auction colluders announced by the Fair Trade Commission on Nov 11.

opeds_today.headline: How Lax Enforcement in Laos Undermines Security on the Korean Peninsula
opeds_today.central_argument: Because Laos serves as a hub for North Korean cyber operators who are easier to pressure than those in China or Russia, US and South Korean authorities should prioritize targeting this Southeast Asian node to disrupt the DPRK IT-worker revenue scheme.
opeds_today.summary: Young argues that North Korean IT workers operating from Laos, which is far more susceptible to US and ROK diplomatic pressure than Beijing or Moscow, represent a high-priority target for disrupting the DPRK's estimated $250-600 million annual IT-worker revenue scheme. The March 2026 Treasury sanctioning of Yun Song Guk, a North Korean IT worker unit leader based in Boten, Laos, is cited as a template for action. The piece connects to broader concerns about North Korean cyber capacity following the $6.36 billion Binance hack.

opeds_today.headline: Trump Is Facing a Very Different North Korea
opeds_today.central_argument: The North Korea that Trump now faces is fundamentally different from the one he engaged in 2018-2019, having expanded its nuclear arsenal, formalized a two-state framework in its constitution, and deepened strategic ties with Russia.
opeds_today.summary: The Foreign Affairs piece argues that the DPRK Kim Jong Un now leads, with an expanded nuclear program, the March 2026 constitutional revision formalizing the two-state framework, and deep Russia entanglement, presents far more constrained diplomatic space for a potential Trump-Kim engagement than existed during 2018-2019. Trump's August 2026 Truth Social post announcing scaled-back US-ROK exercises, citing his 'very good relationship with Kim Jong Un,' is examined as a signal of the president's intent. The piece is directly relevant to today's NK News reporting on how Democratic control of Congress could limit any deal's scope.

opeds_today.headline: One Year After Busan: Has China Kept Its Rare Earth Promises?
opeds_today.central_argument: One year after the Busan Agreement, China's rare earth exports to the United States remain substantially below pre-restriction levels and have declined sharply to both the US and Japan, demonstrating Beijing's continued strategic leverage over critical mineral supply chains despite successive diplomatic agreements.
opeds_today.summary: The CSIS analysis finds that Chinese rare earth exports to the United States remain well below levels recorded before Beijing imposed sweeping export restrictions in April 2025, despite the Geneva, London, and Busan Agreements intended to restore supplies. While China's overall controlled rare earth shipments have remained relatively stable, the selective reduction to the US and Japan suggests continued strategic discretion. With the broader US-China trade truce expiring January 10 2027, the report asks whether Washington can convert diplomatic agreements into reliable access or whether Beijing will continue weaponizing critical mineral dominance.

top_articles.headline: DPRK intelligence officer in China privately concedes North Korea carried out the $6.3 billion Binance hack, contradicting Kim Yo Jong's public denials
top_articles.summary: A North Korean Reconnaissance and Intelligence General Bureau officer based in Liaoning Province told a Daily NK source he believes his own country carried out the November 2026 Binance cryptocurrency heist, directly contradicting Kim Yo Jong's repeated public denials.

senior_officials.name: Kim Yo Jong
senior_officials.role: Vice Director, Korean Workers' Party Central Committee
senior_officials.activity: Kim Yo Jong rejected UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres's call for inter-Korean dialogue after the DMZ landmine incident, accusing him of siding with Seoul, per Reuters and Yonhap citing KCNA, as reported Nov 10 and carried over in today's feeds.

kcna_delta.bottom_line: State media confirmed the publication of the revised constitution's full text formalizing Kim's expanded powers and the two-state framework, while the North Korean ballistic missile launches from Muncheon remain absent from domestic KCNA output.

capitol_hill.headline: Lame-duck Congress opens; National Defense Authorization Act, North Korea bills, and committee chair changes on agenda
capitol_hill.body_text: The lame-duck session of Congress has opened with the National Defense Authorization Act, North Korea-related bills, and committee chair transitions all in play as Democrats prepare to assume majority control in January, per VOA Korean.

capitol_hill.headline: House Republicans quash effort to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth
capitol_hill.body_text: House Republicans blocked a Democratic effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth; Hegseth stated the impeachment attempt was a 'political show' and that he fully supports Trump's military operations, per Korea Herald.

capitol_hill.headline: Expert: Democratic control of Congress could slow South Korea's investments in the United States
capitol_hill.body_text: An expert cited by SBS assessed that Democratic control of Congress could complicate or delay South Korean corporate investments in the United States, as Democratic committees may apply greater scrutiny to deals tied to the $350B pledge and the Korea-US Strategic Investment Corporation.

korea_world.headline: Korea and Indonesia seek joint arms exports beyond troubled KF-21 partnership
korea_world.body_text: South Korea's Defense Acquisition Program Administration held a Korea-Indonesia Defense Industry Cooperation Committee meeting on Nov 11, discussing localization, joint development, and joint export of defense products beyond the disputed KF-21 program, per JoongAng and DAPA readouts. The meeting follows a presidential summit that South Korean and Indonesian officials said elevated bilateral defense ties.

korea_world.headline: Poland receives final 2026 shipment of South Korean K2 tanks and K9 howitzers
korea_world.body_text: Poland received its final 2026 delivery of South Korean K2 tanks and K9 self-propelled howitzers for deployment on NATO's eastern flank, per Defense Mirror. The deliveries are part of a multi-year framework contract that has made Poland one of South Korea's largest defense export customers.
